deities.name: Perun
deities.description: Slavic god of thunder and lightning. Protector of warriors and upholder of cosmic law.

deities.name: Dazhbog
deities.description: God of the sun, wealth, and happiness. Progenitor of the Slavic people and son of Svarog.

deities.name: Mokosh
deities.description: Great earth mother and goddess of weaving, fertility, and the fate of women. The only female deity in Vladimir's Kiev pantheon.

deities.name: Veles
deities.description: God of the underworld, cattle, commerce, magic, and wisdom. The eternal rival of Perun.
deities.mythologyPreview: Veles is the great god of the underworld, cattle, commerce, music, magic, and wisdom. He dwells at the roots of the World Tree in the underworld (Nav), contrasting with Perun who reigns in the crown.

deities.name: Rod
deities.description: Primordial creator deity and ancestor of all gods and living beings. Source of all existence.

deities.name: Domovoi
deities.description: The ancestral household spirit and protector of the home. Lives behind the stove and guards the family.

deities.name: Morozko
deities.description: Personification of winter frost and cold. Tests travelers and rewards the virtuous with gifts.

deities.name: Zorya
deities.description: Twin dawn goddesses representing the morning and evening stars. Guardians of cosmic order and Dazhbog's palace gates.

deities.name: Chernobog
deities.description: God of darkness, evil, and misfortune. Counterpart to the White God, embodying the dark side of cosmic duality.

deities.name: Svarog
deities.description: God of the sky, divine fire, and celestial blacksmithing. Father of Dazhbog. Master craftsman who forged the sun.

deities.name: Marzanna
deities.description: Goddess of winter, death, and seasonal rebirth. Her ritual drowning each spring is one of the most ancient surviving Slavic customs.

deities.name: Baba Yaga
deities.description: Ancient crone witch and guardian of the boundary between the living and the dead. Ambivalent helper and devourer.

deities.name: Kupala and Kupalo
deities.description: Twin sibling deities of the summer solstice, embodying fire, water, and love. Their festival is the most beloved night of the Slavic year.

deities.name: Stribog
deities.description: God of wind, air, and sky. Grandfather of all winds — from the gentlest breeze to the mightiest tempest.

deities.name: Leshy
deities.description: Master spirit of the forest and protector of all wildlife. A shapeshifter who leads trespassers astray.
deities.mythologyPreview: The Leshy is the master spirit of the forest — one of the most powerful nature spirits in Slavic belief. He can appear as a giant whose head touches the treetops, or shrink to the height of a mushroom

deities.name: Rusałka
deities.description: Water spirits and souls of young women who died before marriage. Both beautiful and deadly, they guard the waters and ensure rain for crops.

deities.name: Domovina
deities.description: Personification of the ancestral homeland. Embodies the sacred bond between a people and their land, encompassing both the living and the dead.

deities.name: Jarilo
deities.description: God of spring, vegetation, and the returning sun. His annual arrival brings warmth and fertility to the world.

deities.name: Dolya and Sudba
deities.description: Personifications of personal fate and fortune. Dolya brings luck; Nedolya brings misfortune. Together they weave the thread of each human life.
deities.mythologyPreview: Dolya (Good Fate) and Nedolya (Bad Fate/Misfortune) are personified fate-spirits assigned to each person at birth. Dolya is a beautiful young woman who follows the lucky person, while Nedolya is a hag

deities.name: Simargl
deities.description: Sacred winged dog-dragon and guardian of seeds and sacred fire. Listed among the gods of Vladimir's Kiev pantheon.

deities.name: Veleslav
deities.description: Venerable figure of ancient wisdom connected to the Veles cult. Keeper of ancestral knowledge and oral tradition.

deities.name: Zhiva
deities.description: Goddess of life, living nature, and vital force. The divine counterpart to Marzanna whose reign begins when winter dies.
deities.mythologyPreview: Zhiva (the Alive One) is the goddess of life, living nature, and vital force. She is the divine embodiment of vitality — the force that animates all living things. She is the counterpart and rival to

deities.name: Divi
deities.description: Spirit of wild, untamed nature. A primal force beyond human civilization, bringing omens and awe-inspiring power.
deities.mythologyPreview: Div (Wild One) is the spirit of untamed, primordial nature — the force of pure wilderness. He is mentioned in the Tale of Igor's Campaign as a supernatural omen-being that cries disaster from the tree

deities.name: Triglav
symbols: Three heads (or one head with three faces)
deities.description: The three-headed deity ruling sky, earth, and underworld simultaneously. Worshipped by Baltic Slavic tribes with a sacred black horse used for divination.

deities.name: Zhivini Pole
deities.description: The Slavic paradise — a mythical sunlit meadow of eternal spring where righteous souls rest between lives.

deities.name: Roda
deities.description: Birth goddess associated with Rod. She and the Rozhanitsy appear at every birth to weave the fate and life path of the newborn.

deities.name: Yasen
deities.description: Divine guardian of the ash tree and spirit of spring's return to the forest. Governs healing and the World Tree.

deities.name: Lada
deities.description: Goddess of beauty, love, harmony, and marriage. Her name echoes in ancient Slavic ritual songs sung across all Slavic lands.
deities.mythologyPreview: Lada is the goddess of beauty, love, harmony, marriage, and spring. Her name is the root of the Slavic word 'lad' — harmony, order, and peace. She appears as a radiant young woman crowned with flowers

deities.name: Dnipro
deities.description: Divine personification of the great Dnieper River — the sacred lifeblood of Eastern Slavic civilization and trade.

deities.name: Dobrovij
deities.description: Deity of goodness, kindness, and moral virtue. Divine endorsement of generosity and right action.
deities.mythologyPreview: Dobrovij (The Good One) is a benevolent deity of goodness, kindness, and moral virtue. His name derives from 'dobro' — the Slavic root for goodness, one of the most positively charged words in Slavic
